The same predeclared seeds, search parameters and 30-minute cap were then run in an optimized build on one nice19 pinned CPU; exit marker 0, zero stderr bytes. All 64 seeds have exactly one game in each root seat. Complete BatchObservation and legal-action order were asserted equal before every counterfactual query. Code CI passed Rust formatting, Clippy -D warnings, workspace tests and WASM; Python/web CI also passed.
interpretation: The exploratory point result favors planning with the live hidden RNG, but the independent-map two-sided sign p is 0.061 and the effect is not positive in both seats. This does not establish a robust complete-game advantage, a global Elo, or that hidden RNG caused the rejected neural student's failure. The separate same-observation audit proved search labels can differ with hidden RNG; this game result limits the strength claim for one fixed planning perturbation. No search parameter, game rule, student, rated bot or playable Site was changed.
